### policy_self_consistency (this task only)

Policies this task exercises (derived, not read from charter_scope): root `line_ext_close_to_draws_payment` (C); prerequisites `line_ext_returned_payment_fee` (R), `line_ext_draw_fee` (D), `line_ext_draw_fee_error_credit` (E).

Handling time (check 4): each write is evaluated on `initial_state` + the earlier writes of this task (table in task_independent_derivation). No formula reads a value a later write produces.

Real-world waits (check 5): every input is a seeded row (`line_transactions`, `credit_lines`, `loans`, `loan_transactions`) or the DB effect of an earlier write in this task. No payment clearing, approval or date advance is consumed. Exception — see CG-1 below: on one defensible reading of the charter the root write itself has to wait for the returned-payment freeze to lift (not before 2026-10-19).

Charter-global defects that bear on this task, consequence demonstrated on this world:

- **CG-1 (frozen line)** — `credit_lines.7e35858e….status = frozen`, `freeze_reason = returned_payment`. The base lifecycle and the `line_closed_to_draws` event allow the borrower's close-to-draws only `from: active`. `line_evt_freeze` keeps a line frozen for a returned payment until "the current date is later than the return date plus the returned-payment freeze days" (return `96dcc7d3…` dated 2026-10-08, Standard `returned_payment_freeze_days` 10, so not before 2026-10-19). Reading 1 (rule "A borrower may close the line at any time"): close today; C writes. Reading 2 (lifecycle/event `from: active`): the line cannot be closed to draws while frozen; the agent declines or tells the customer to come back after the freeze lifts. Neither the base nor C's rule says which governs a frozen line. Two defensible terminal states: line in `repayment` with a payment recorded, or no change.
- **CG-2 (undeclared override: level repayment payment)** — base `line_evt_payments_and_fees`: "in repayment it is the level repayment payment plus any amount past due". Base variant parameter `repayment_payment_method`: "level payment amortizing the balance … at the APR in force". Event `line_closed_to_draws` field `minimum_payment_due: Level repayment-period payment.` On this world C's method factor picks the equal-share method (tier 1), so the payment is not a level payment. With every other C factor as derived, the level-payment reading gives **118.61** and C's rule gives **141.96** (`/tmp` recomputation, substitution C5 below).
- **CG-7 (payment-sizing rate is not the APR charged)** — on this world the APR used is 24.74 + 0.25 − 0.50 = **24.49** while the line keeps accruing at `line_apr` 24.74; the close tool does not change `line_apr`. With the level method, 30 payments of 118.61 on 2641.60 leave **13.91** unpaid at 24.74%. So the rule's "level payment that repays the balance over that number of months" is false here.
- **CG-8 (accrued interest folded in)** — tier 1 is taken: 23 days of unbilled interest (40.55) go into the amount repaid. Base `line_evt_interest_and_annual_fee` still bills those same days at the next statement closing (base "Interest is charged at each statement closing on the average daily balance of the cycle"), so the borrower is charged interest for 2026-09-24..10-16 twice.
- **CG-6 (credit larger than the fee it waives)** — E books a lender_error `line_fee_waived` entry of **41.51** against the 30.00 draw-fee entry `8d047365…`.
- **CG-4 / CG-5 (unreal factor conditions/values)** — tiers taken on this world that belong to those classes: C `accrued_interest_treatment` (AutoPay-selected), D `back_billing_relief` (1.00, AutoPay-selected), D `personal_loan_fee_credit` (1.00), R `standing_credit` (0.50, AutoPay-selected), R `loan_relationship_credit` (1.00), E `service_recovery_amount` (5.00), E `autopay_courtesy_amount` (1.00), E `personal_loan_goodwill` (2.00), E `extra_entry_rebate` (3.00). Each one moves a scored value (factor_weight), so the scored values carry the invented mechanics.
- **CG-3 (mislabelled method)** — E's only `method` factor, `interest_putback_method`, takes tier 1 here: 30.00 × 24.74/36500 × 25 days. Tier 2 would be 30.00 × 24.74/1200. That is the same formula with a different period, so E has no honest method factor.

The earlier return `9376ce53…` has its fee `c6920c3b…`. | R (`assess_returned_payment_fee_0fd8e99d`) | value_input (conversion balance) |
| 2 | "The repayment payment is not fixed until each draw on the line carries a draw-fee entry, wherever the tier charges a draw fee." | draw `c122aa76…` (2026-10-05, 400.00) has no `line_draw_fee_assessed` row. Standard `draw_fee_percent` is 2.5 > 0. | D (`assess_draw_fee_4f046c6c`) | value_input (conversion balance) |
| 3 | "Before the repayment payment is worked out, any draw carrying more than one draw-fee entry must also carry a fee-waiver entry for each extra draw-fee entry." | draw `8d66a7e6…` (2026-08-28, 1200.00) carries `aa5788fb…` (08-28, 30.00) and `8d047365…` (08-29, 30.00). No `line_fee_waived` row relates to either. | E (`credit_draw_fee_error_e1e6ecd0`) | value_input (conversion balance) |

D's rule carries "A back-billed draw fee is fixed only after every draw-fee entry charged twice on the line carries a fee-waiver entry for the extra charge." That is false at the opening for the same reason as row 3, so there is an edge D ← E (value_input: E's lender_error waiver turns on D's back-billing relief). R's and E's rules carry no prerequisite sentence.

- Derived tree: C ← {R, D, E}; D ← E. Three prerequisite problems, four value_input edges (needed: max(3−1,1) = 2). Acyclic. The owner=user write is C (`close_line_to_draws_7539d675`, `@tool(owner="user")`). The persona hands it over: "when they hand you the step to close the line yourself, you carry it out".
- Topological order: E → D → C, with R anywhere before C. The writes of R and of the E/D pair only add to the balance; neither reads the other (R reads return/late-fee/AutoPay/loan rows, D reads draw/late-fee/waiver/loan rows, E reads draw-fee/statement/payment/draw/loan rows). - Tool layer: none of the eight function bodies checks a prerequisite, a status or a freeze. Each one only `ctx.find`s the line, `ctx.create`s a row and/or `ctx.update`s fields (`task_tools.py` lines 11–299).
- Isomorphism with the author's declared tree: the `prerequisite` fields of C (R, D, E, all value_input, gate `conversion_balance`) and D (E, value_input, gate `back_billing_relief`) match the derived tree exactly.

## findings

**F-0a SOURCE-TASK RED (from CG-1) — a frozen line's close-to-draws has two defensible outcomes.**
- Symptom: GT closes a `frozen` line today. The base lifecycle and event allow a borrower's close only from `active`.
- Root cause: CG-1 (`_difficulty.md` § findings).
- Evidence:
  - `initial_state.credit_lines.7e35858e-b82c-4056-a1ce-349d7b3fa3fc.status = frozen`, `freeze_reason = returned_payment`;
  - line.extended.yaml lifecycle `{from: active, to: repayment, by: user}`; event `line_closed_to_draws` `mutation: {transition: {from: active, to: repayment}}`;
  - base freeze sentence (not unfreezable before 2026-10-19);
  - base rule "A borrower may close the line at any time".
- Consequence: reading 2 writes nothing today (refuse, or ask her to call back after the freeze lifts) against GT's C = 141.96 written today.
- Affected: base lifecycle/event and `line_evt_draw_period_and_closure`; C's rule; GT steps unlock_user/call_user close.
- Previous revisions: first audit.

**F-0b SOURCE-POLICY/SOURCE-TASK RED (from CG-2) — undeclared departure from the level repayment payment.**
- Evidence: base `line_evt_payments_and_fees` "in repayment it is the level repayment payment plus any amount past due"; variant `repayment_payment_method`; event field "Level repayment-period payment."; C's overwrite retires only the draw-period-end sentence.
- Consequence on this world: level reading 118.61 (all other factors as derived) vs GT 141.96.
- Affected: C `overwrite`; GT `repayment_payment`.

**F-0c SOURCE-FACTOR RED (from CG-7, CG-8) — C's payment rests on a non-APR rate and double-billed interest.**
- The rate used is 24.49 while the line accrues at 24.74. On the level method this leaves 13.91 unpaid after 30 months.
- 40.55 of unbilled interest for 2026-09-24..10-16 is folded into the amount repaid and also billed at the next closing under base `line_evt_interest_and_annual_fee`.
- The `return_addon`, `relationship_reduction` and `accrued_interest_treatment` contributions to 141.96 are those mechanics: their substitutions give 141.41, 143.06 and 139.78.

**F-0d SOURCE-FACTOR RED (from CG-3, CG-4, CG-5, CG-6) — the prerequisite computations carry invented mechanics.**
- E = 41.51 against a 30.00 fee (CG-6).
- 11.00 of E, 2.00 of D's credits and 1.50 of R's credits are CG-5 members.
- E's only method factor is mislabelled (CG-3).
- AutoPay-selected tiers: D relief, R standing credit, E courtesy, C accrued interest (CG-4).
- After striking, E has 0 factors, R 2, D 2, C 3, all below the 4–6 bound.

**F-0e SOURCE-TASK RED (XF-14 proof text) — two stale assertions.**
1. `evaluation_criteria` step `find_loan_transactions`, necessity: "the returned-payment fee's relationship credit counts personal-loan returned payments in the last 12 months". R's rule and compute (`loan_autopay_12m`: XCOUNT `loan_payment_posted` with `payment_channel='autopay_ach'`) count personal-loan AutoPay payments, not returns. The rationale's own REVISIONS (2) records that switch.
2. `design_rationale` SCOPE and problem-tree card E3: "the task-1 fee-error waiver is scoped to late and returned-payment fees" / "a late/returned-fee error waiver". W's rule covers only "a late fee charged for a due date whose minimum payment had posted in full …"; returned-payment fees charged in error stay under the base clause.
- Neither changes a scored value. Both are false statements in the proof.
